note: What the creatures do, the routes through this place, and what a Remix may change.

locked: Core problem: Memories manifest as voices and scenes; truth and false inference become difficult to separate.
Regional identity: ... drowned bell towers, echoing sea caves.
open: The harpies' Luring Song uses the voices the drowned bell has kept, so a charmed character hears a friend calling from the shallows.
The party must cross the tide flats to reach the belfry (EC-BC-03) and the cliff stair (EC-BC-05).

original.does: Roosts on the belfry and the tall stones; sings the Luring Song with the bell's stolen voices; flies down to claw the lured.
Lies in the rock pools and rises when the song starts; grapples whoever the song draws into the shallows.

difficulty.tuner_recommends: one fewer Giant Crab (plays as moderate); not applied: the GM has not decided

terrain.water: rock pools across the tide flats; the belfry stands in the shallows
terrain.flight: open sky everywhere but the echo cave (12 ft, lowering to 6 ft)
rewards: creatures that pull characters into the water
terrain.gaps: no narrow passages on the flats; the echo cave mouth is 15 ft wide

may_change: the read-aloud and GM lines about them
must_keep: the bell's kept voices as what lures or misleads the party
the crossing to the belfry and the stair
the measured difficulty (plays as high, or the GM's chosen target)

filters.movement: a swimmer or a flier fits the map best; walkers only in the mix

remix.freshness: a remix for returning players avoids Harpies and Giant Crabs

routes.when: Once the first voice calls from the shallows, before anyone is charmed.
routes.success: The singer answers in the same voices and the harpies' song loses them: the bell falls quiet, the harpies circle and screech but only attack a character who wades into the shallows, and the crabs stay in their pools. The party crosses the flats.
routes.failure: The song swells over the singer's voice: the fight starts as written, and the singer has Disadvantage on its first saving throw against the Luring Song.
lines: Harpy, in a borrowed sailor's voice: 'Come down to the boats, love, the tide is in!'
Harpy, when the song breaks: 'Thief! Those are our voices!'
routes.reveals: The voices the harpies use are real people from the old quay: names cried as ships came in, the people who came by sea.
routes.canon: Shows the core problem in play: real memories, used to mislead.

routes.when: A character speaks to the harpies before the song starts (they speak Common and are vain about their singing).
routes.condition_alt: Or a gift they want: Rusk's catch from the boat, or something that shines.
routes.success: The harpies let the party cross to the cliff stair and watch from the belfry. Their price: no one touches the bell, because it calls the sailors they feed on.
routes.failure: They laugh and begin to sing: the fight starts as written.
routes.cost: The bell's memories (EC-BC-03) now break the bargain: touching the bell starts this fight in the belfry.
lines: Harpy: 'The bell is ours. It sings, they come. You may pass, little walkers, if you leave our bell alone.'
routes.reveals: The harpies know the bell repeats only what was once said near it, and that it never says anything new.
routes.later: If the party touches the bell anyway, the harpies attack in EC-BC-03 (same creatures, the crabs rising from the shallows around the stump).
routes.canon: The party chooses between a safe crossing and the memories: a small version of the chapter's moral question about useful stories and evidence.

routes.when: Anyone who sees a crab move in the pools, or has fish or meat to throw.
routes.success: Fish thrown into the far pools draw the crabs away: they join the fight only on the third round, if it comes to one.
routes.failure: The crabs come for the food and the thrower: they rise at once and close on the party.
routes.reveals: Nothing new: the crabs are only hungry.
routes.canon: Does not change the story job; it shrinks the fight.

routes.when: The party keeps to the cliff foot, out of the pools, toward the stair.
routes.success: The party reaches the cliff stair unseen (the harpies' Passive Perception is 10, the crabs' 9). The song starts only if someone goes out to the belfry.
routes.failure: A harpy spots them halfway: the fight starts with the party strung out along the cliff foot.
routes.cost: The belfry's memories wait in the shallows: going out to them later wakes the encounter.
routes.reveals: Nothing new on the way; the bell strikes once as the tide turns.
routes.canon: The clue room is still there to visit; nothing is skipped for good.

routes.when: In the echo cave (EC-BC-04), after Selric tests it, someone looks for another way up.
routes.success: A sea ledge runs from the cave mouth round the cliff to the foot of the stair, out of the harpies' sight: the party skips the tide flats and the belfry.
routes.failure: The ledge ends in a sheer drop; the party comes back to the flats having lost time.
routes.clue_elsewhere: EC-BC-04 the echo cave shows the same trick in small (Selric: 'It does not lie. It edits.'), and the chapter's later rooms (the crystal maze, the amphitheater, the memory palace) carry the core problem on.
routes.reveals: From the ledge the party sees the harpies' roost and the bell from above: the bell's rim is crusted with offerings, not shells.
routes.canon: The core problem is still delivered by the echo cave and the rest of the chapter.
